items.title: Louis Armstrong: Jazz Casual Interview, 1964-07-10
items.q: And like I played on the excursion boats with Fate Marables band. That was a good band, 1919 to 1921.

ctx.x: But that was really the first thing that I lost the memory.

Well, that was my life. That's all I knew of. Sure. But you have to get with different. Now like when I went with Fletcher Anderson's band in 1924. Well, there was something else. There was Don Richmond. The minute I get up on the stand to join the band, there's a part in front of me. You know, well, I was at least tall. And you get conscious. You know, your mind, as you go along, you've got to get with it. Yeah. So you lose something. But is that all good experience for you as a musician? I enjoy the experience.…

So all this added to your own equipment as a truck. As a truck. Yeah. And I didn't try to do nothing else but blows. And you would advise any youngster today to, I would assume, to have as much experience as a concert?

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1962-09-19
items.q: before I got on the steam of Sydney, where Fate Marable used to play the Calypies and things.

ctx.x: And when you got on the riverboats, what was the life like?

Well, it's just the idea that I was on a nicer boat, because I knew the life of riverboats before I got on the steam of Sydney, where Fate Marable used to play the Calypies and things. But before that, we used to unload cotton boats, banana boats. See? I always had the idea of boats, but this was like a dance hall, an excursion boat. And when I got in that band, I kind of feel like I'm a little high up on the horse, you know? You're a composer too, though. Yeah, I wrote a lot of tunes. I wrote Wish I Could Stream…
But how do tunes come to you? How do you compose?
